items.title: Police arrest UK man at airport months after armed Mississauga carjacking
items.summary: A 24-year-old man from the United Kingdom has been arrested after Peel Regional Police allege he fled Canada following an armed carjacking in Mississauga earlier this year. According to investigators, the suspect returned to Toronto on an international flight on July 16 and was arrested upon landing at Pearson Airport on an outstanding Canada-wide warrant. The charges stem from a carjacking that occurred on Feb. m. in the area of Torbram Road and Derry Road East. Police say the victim was sitting inside a commercial vehicle when two masked suspects approached armed with handguns. The suspects allegedly pointed the firearms at the victim before forcing him from the vehicle and stealing it. Following an investigation by Peel Regional Police’s Central Robbery Bureau, officers identified Raheem Hartley, 24, of the United Kingdom, as one of the alleged suspects. Investigators say Hartley left Canada shortly after the carjacking. A Canada-wide warrant for his arrest was issued in December 2025 after police determined he had fled the country. When Hartley returned to Canada on July 16, officers arrested him at Toronto Pearson International Airport. Hartley has been charged with robbery, disguise with intent, and use of an imitation firearm while committing an offence.

items.title: House of the week: Family home near Rattray Marsh in Mississauga
items.summary: This place: A family home near Rattray Marsh in Mississauga. 4-acre lot surrounded by mature trees, landscaping and an in-ground pool, this cherished family home offers privacy and comfort in sought-after Clarkson. Large windows fill the home with natural light. The eat-in kitchen features a pantry, prep space and walkout access to the backyard. There are two fireplaces on the main floor, and the layout flows between the living, dining and family spaces. A main-floor laundry room with direct mudroom and garage access completes the level. Upstairs, the four bedrooms each have their own closet. The primary bedroom offers a walk-in closet and a three-piece ensuite bathroom. The basement features a recreation area, fireplace, dry bar and storage space. The home is close to lakefront trails in the Rattray Marsh Conservation Area, shops and cafes in Clarkson Village and Port Credit. Thanks to Sam McDadi Real Estate Inc. items.title: Heat warning slows down express trains at Toronto Pearson Airport in Mississauga
items.summary: Passengers riding Union Pearson Express trains between Mississauga and Toronto on Friday afternoon might notice several delays due to a heat warning issued by Canada’s weather agency, transit officials say. The UP Express moves passengers between Toronto Pearson Airport in Mississauga and Union Station in downtown Toronto. Transit officials said to customers in an online post that “a heat warning from Environment Canada is in effect today. We are required to run trains at slower speeds. m. ” UP Express officials have also given a heads-up to customers that the trains will be replaced by GO buses the weekend of Aug. 15-16 due to planned construction on the line. When operating without delays, the express trains transport riders between Canada’s biggest and busiest airport and Union Station in downtown Toronto in just under 30 minutes, making several stops along the way. m. between downtown Toronto and Pearson. Officials at Metrolinx said earlier the express train service “has become an integral part of transit in Toronto, having served more than 26 million passengers” since its inception in 2015. In what at the time was the “first dedicated express air-rail link service in North America,” the UP Express took its first passengers between Pearson and Union Station in downtown Toronto on June 6, 2015, Ontario transit officials said earlier.

items.title: Two centuries of history: Leslie Log House celebrates 200 years
items.summary: Built in 1826, the Leslie Log House remains a treasured link to Mississauga's early settlement history. Entertainment and activities | July 31, 2026 Members of the media and public are invited to attend a special celebration marking the 200th anniversary of the Leslie Log House, one of the oldest remaining log homes in Ontario. The event will recognize the site’s historical significance and its role in preserving Mississauga’s early settler history. m. m. Community programming continues including a tea room, art in the park and more! Members of Council, representatives from the City of Mississauga and the Streetsville Historical Society, along with community members and heritage enthusiasts. Built in 1826, the Leslie Log House is one of the oldest surviving log homes in Ontario and a designated heritage property. Operated in partnership with the Streetsville Historical Society, the house offers visitors a glimpse into life in early Upper Canada and serves as an important reminder of Mississauga’s rural and agricultural roots. items.title: Student entrepreneurs gear up for IDEA Connect Summer Market
items.summary: From custom nails and baked goods to creative media, Mississauga's young business owners have something for everyone. On August 12, the IDEA Connect Summer Market will present an event at IDEA Square One that features 13 student-run businesses. Visitors can shop for unique products and services, meet the young business owners behind them and support local talent. The event is a chance to connect, discover something new and celebrate the next generation of entrepreneurs. The young business owners are part of Summer Company, a program funded by the Government of Ontario. People ages 15 to 29 start and run their own businesses during the summer months. High school students commit to 280 or more hours while post-secondary students commit to 420 or more hours between May and Labour Day. Through training, guidance from IDEA and hands-on experience, they build skills and turn their ideas into real businesses. The IDEA Connect Summer Market takes place at the end of the IDEA Mississauga Summer Company program. Students get to meet customers and get sales experience before heading back to school. The IDEA Connect Summer Market features 13 student-run businesses that are part of the Summer Company program in Mississauga. Visitors can shop for goods and services at the market. They’ll get a passport and collect a stamp as they visit each business. They can enter their stamped passports into a raffle to win an IDEA gift bag.
